observations.behavior: Adds a new utility to compare current URL filters against saved dashboard state and determine if an override is active.
observations.posthog_connection: This could help PostHog dashboards avoid showing unnecessary "overrides" warnings when clearing filters without changing the actual query. This improves UX for users who want to clear saved parameters.

observations.behavior: Adds tests checking that empty overrides are preserved only when they change saved values; otherwise removed.
observations.posthog_connection: These checks support reliability of the filtering behavior by preventing edge cases where clearing a filter leaves stale or incorrect URL params.

observations.behavior: Uses deep equality comparison rather than loose object identity or shallow comparison.
observations.posthog_connection: Using strict equality helps prevent false positives in detecting changes between complex nested structures like property filters, improving correctness of the override detection.

observations.limitations: Only frontend TypeScript and its unit tests were provided; no backend implementation or migration compatibility was shown. The tier depends on whether this logic actually prevents user-visible issues or merely refactors existing behavior.

review.limitations: Only frontend TypeScript and its unit tests were provided; no backend implementation or migration compatibility was shown. The tier depends on whether this logic actually prevents user-visible issues or merely refactors existing behavior.
review.reason: The chunk adds a bounded capability: distinguishing whether URL-based filter overrides meaningfully differ from saved dashboard filters. Tests cover preservation and removal rules. It does not demonstrate broader systemic risk reduction across components, so it cannot reach tier 3.
review.posthog_relevance: Could help PostHog dashboards avoid showing unnecessary "overrides" warnings when clearing filters without changing the actual query. This improves UX for users who want to clear saved parameters.
review.uncertainty: This is a single-file change with no test execution results or production context. Its real benefit could depend on how widely the previous heuristic caused incorrect UI states.
